Louise Lucas, has been indicted alongside six others, including members of her family, over an alleged racketeering conspiracy involving the illegal sale of marijuana and money laundering. item.title: TUC not part of FG talks, issued no ultimatum, NLC clarifies
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, has clarified that the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria, TUC, neither issued an ultimatum to the Federal Government nor participated in the dialogue between the government and the NLC held on October 22, 2026. The clarification follows media reports that mentioned the TUC in connection with the ultimatum and the meeting, prompting the NLC to set the record straight and absolve the sister labour centre of any involvement in the specific engagement. In a statement signed by its Acting General Secretary, Comrade Benson Upah, the NLC said the TUC’s name was erroneously included in some newspaper reports, while acknowledging that a greater number of publications correctly attributed the statement to the NLC alone. The statement reads: “The Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) wishes to clarify that the Trade Union Congress (TUC) did not issue an ultimatum to the government and was not part of the dialogue between the NLC and Federal Government yesterday, 22nd October 2026 even as the TUC side of Joint Health Workers Union of Nigeria, JOHESU and Joint Public Service Negotiating Council, JPSNC were represented at the dialogue. “TUC’s name featured in error in a paper or two but we note that a greater number of the papers appropriately attributed the statement to NLC only. “This is to categorically state that only the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) was present at the meeting. “The TUC is completely exonerated from the purports of this specific dialogue. We urge the public and media to take note of this correction, please.” The post TUC not part of FG talks, issued no ultimatum, NLC clarifies appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Man Utd defeat to Como ‘unacceptable’, says Carrick
item.description: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick admitted on Friday his side have “lost their way” after a 4-1 thrashing by Champions League debutants Como made it seven games without a win. After a successful interim spell in charge in the second half of last season, Carrick was appointed on a permanent basis just five months ago, but his position is at risk ahead of Sunday’s visit of Bournemouth to Old Trafford. United are off to their worst start in the Premier League era, were dumped out of the League Cup by Brighton and have lost two of their opening three Champions League games. “Recently we haven’t had a good time. I totally accept that. We had five months of relative success in a spell where I was happy with a lot of things we were doing as a team,” Carrick said in an impassioned address at the start of his press conference on Friday. “We haven’t done well enough lately. We’ve had a spell we’re really not happy with. Como was a bad night. It hurt me. It was really unacceptable. “The supporters have to make the effort and spend the money to come and watch us. To have the feeling we all had after the game was a tough moment.” Carrick added: “My job is to put a team on the pitch that represents the supporters and that they can be proud of the identity we show. We have gone away from that recently in certain games which I am fully aware of and definintely doing something about.” AFP The post Man Utd defeat to Como ‘unacceptable’, says Carrick appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: I once wanted to be a DJ – UK’s Prince William
item.description: Prince William has made a rare royal appearance on a BBC chat show, with the heir to the throne confessing he would have liked to join the police or be a DJ. The Prince of Wales appeared on an episode set to air Friday evening, to promote his Earthshot Prize, which goes to environmental causes. The show’s host, comedian Graham Norton, is known for his A-list guests and mildly ribbing celebrities. Wearing a blue suit, shirt and tie, William was roaring with laughter in images released ahead of the show on his and his wife’s Instagram. He sat on the show’s sofa next to actresses Cate Blanchett and Hannah Waddingham and conservationist Robert Irwin, all involved in the prize. Hello! magazine wrote that William is the first working royal to appear on a British talk show although Sarah Ferguson, the former wife of William’s uncle, the former prince Andrew, was interviewed by Norton when she still had a royal title. The Graham Norton Show is now in its 33rd series and is the broadcaster’s most watched chat show. Recent guests include Madonna. The BBC reported there were “cheers and gasps from the audience” when William appeared as a surprise guest. He will present the Earthshot Prize in Mumbai on November 17. Launched in 2020, the prize supports initiatives that help tackle environmental crises such as climate change. As with previous competitions, this year’s winners will receive one million pounds ($1.3 million) each “to accelerate the impact of their innovative solutions”, organisers said. William was asked whether he ever fantasised about another job rather than becoming king, telling Norton: “I did want to be a policeman when I was younger. I thought I could make a good one,” adding that he also went through “a phase of wanting to be a DJ — I wasn’t very good.” William spoke of his family’s love for “The Celebrity Traitors”, a devious reality show currently topping ratings. He also said he was a “big fan” of director Christopher Nolan’s “Dark Knight” trilogy about Batman, which he called “psychologically dark and deep”. The prince has kept tight-lipped about the return to Britain of his estranged brother Prince Harry, who said in an interview this week with GQ magazine that he wanted things to “work out” with his father, King Charles III, and William, his elder brother. item.title: Malaria: Nigeria’s prevalence drops to 15.2%, FG targets 50% reduction by 2030
item.description: By Chioma Obinna The Federal Government has reported a decline in malaria parasite prevalence among children aged six to 59 months from 22 per cent in 2021 to 15.2 per cent in 2025, while setting a target to halve malaria prevalence and malaria-attributable deaths by 2030. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, disclosed this on Thursday at the launch of the 2025 Nigeria Malaria Indicator Survey (NMIS) Report and the National Malaria Strategic Plan 2026–2030 in Abuja. Pate, who was represented by the ministry’s Permanent Secretary, Daju Kachollom, said the 6.8 percentage-point decline reflected progress in the country’s malaria control efforts but warned that the gains must be sustained. He said the Federal Government was targeting a 50 per cent reduction in malaria prevalence and malaria-attributable deaths from their respective 2025 levels by 2030. The minister, however, cautioned against interpreting the decline as evidence that malaria had been brought under control nationwide, stressing the need for stronger prevention, surveillance and funding. He cited Kebbi State as an example of significant improvement, with malaria prevalence reportedly dropping from 49 per cent in 2021 to 18 per cent in 2025. Pate said the findings underscored the importance of using reliable data to identify high-burden communities and direct interventions where they would have the greatest impact. Bed-net use remains a concern The minister also highlighted the need to improve the consistent use of insecticide-treated nets, a major tool for preventing malaria transmission. According to the survey findings, 72.3 per cent of children and 80.6 per cent of pregnant women in households that owned insecticide-treated nets slept under one. item.title: Ogogo’s daughters announce Nollywood plans, pledge to sustain father’s legacy
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The daughters of late Nollywood actor Taiwo Hassan, popularly known as Ogogo, say they plan to pursue careers in the film industry and continue their father’s legacy. Taiwo Halima Olamide, known as Lima Ogogo, and her sister, Shakirat Taiwo, popularly called Kira Ogogo, announced their plans in an appreciation video shared on social media on Wednesday, October 21. The sisters also thanked Nigerians and members of the entertainment industry for supporting their family following their father’s death. “You guys loved our daddy so much. This is an appreciation video to tell you people thank you,” they said. Lima, speaking on behalf of the family, added: “On behalf of my family and I, we want to say thank you very much to everybody who stood by us.” The sisters acknowledged support from several public figures, including Honourable Tayo Ayinde, the First Lady, the Ogun State governor, Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, and the Olu of Ilaro. They also thanked those who sent messages of condolence during the family’s period of mourning. They said their entry into Nollywood would be a lasting commitment, rather than a one-off tribute to their father. “We are going to start seeing Ogogo through my sister Kira Ogogo. We are coming to the industry, and we’re here to stay,” Lima said. The sisters urged fans who enjoyed Ogogo’s films to support their upcoming projects by watching and sharing their content, particularly on Kira Ogogo’s YouTube channel, KiraOgogoTV. Ogogo, a prominent figure in Yoruba cinema, died on August 23, 2026, aged 66. He was buried the following day in Ilaro, Ogun State, according to Islamic rites. A visa on arrival (VoA) allows eligible travellers to obtain a visa at an authorised airport, seaport or border crossing. item.title: FG Designates Redeemer’s Health Village As TETFund Centre, Guarantees Scholarships For Robotic Surgery Academy
item.description: In a breakthrough for Nigeria’s healthcare sector, the Federal Government has adopted the newly inaugurated Redeemer’s Health Village (RHV) Robotic Surgery Academy as the nation’s 29th TETFund Centre of Excellence, guaranteeing full scholarship coverage for all enrolled trainees. Speaking at the official inauguration on Thursday, Minister of Education Dr. Tunji Alausa declared that the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) will fully fund the tuition fees of qualified medical professionals undergoing specialist training at the academy through its local scholarship scheme. ﻿ The strategic partnership — established alongside RoboMed Global, the National Postgraduate Medical College of Nigeria (NPMCN), and Redeemer’s University — establishes Nigeria’s pioneer institute for advanced robotic and telesurgical operations. ₦250bn Healthcare Injection Highlighting the government’s drive to curb brain drain and eliminate foreign medical tourism, Alausa disclosed that the Federal Government has injected over ₦250 billion into medical education across the last two years. “The same number of medical students admitted while I was in medical school is the same number we have maintained over the years, without sufficient consideration of our population growth,” the minister stated, confirming plans to expand annual medical programme enrolments to 20,000 within two years. By designating RHV as a Special Centre of Excellence, TETFund sponsorship will ensure that financial barriers do not stop top clinical talent from acquiring cutting-edge surgical skills locally. $4m Infrastructure The newly launched academy hits the ground running with $4 million worth of dual robotic surgical systems, designed to power both clinical service delivery and high-level training. According to RHV Chief Executive Officer Adedamola Dada, the academy aims to produce 400 certified specialists within two years across three main specialties: Urology, General Surgery, and Gynaecology. The academy’s scope extends beyond doctors to train an entire technical ecosystem, including operating theatre personnel, biomedical engineers, and hospital administrators. RHV also recently achieved full accreditation as an academic medical school. Co-founder of RoboMed Global, Dr. Obi Ekwenna, emphasised that the academy relies on a total-ecosystem training model inspired by aviation safety standards prioritizing communication, simulation, and strict team coordination. “The essence of the academy is to train the entire ecosystem, not just surgeons alone,” Ekwenna noted, explaining that candidate evaluation will blend advanced simulation, supervised clinical practice, and structured patient care. item.title: Jide Kosoko laments debt as N300m cinema film fails to make profit
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Veteran Nollywood actor and filmmaker Jide Kosoko says he is in debt after his film, Eleko: Oba Esugbayi , failed to recoup its production cost of more than N300 million at the cinemas. Kosoko made the disclosure in a recent interview with African A-List, saying the film was financed by investors who expected returns, not money given to him as a gift. “My film ‘Eleko: Oba Esugbayi’ that recently came out and we took to the cinemas, cost us over N300 million. Do I have 300 million? You should know that some people gave it to me and it was not that they dashed me; they invested in it and we took the film to the cinemas,” he said. The filmmaker said the movie did not generate enough revenue to recover the investment. The small amount it earned was shared among those involved in the project. “Different things happened and we did not earn our money back. The little that was earned was split. As I am, if you hear someone with debt dancing around their neck, it is me,” Kosoko said. In another account of the interview, Kosoko was quoted as clarifying that the debt remark was not necessarily a reference to unpaid wages. He said the people who worked on the production had been paid, but the film did not deliver the financial returns he and the investors had hoped for. He also acknowledged the substantial investments made by cinema operators when asked about the film’s cinema earnings and their distribution. “I won’t deceive anyone, but truly, those who own the cinemas have huge investments,” he said. Kosoko’s comments echo concerns raised by actor and filmmaker Ramsey Nouah, who has said that releasing a film in cinemas does not always make financial sense. Nouah said only a small fraction of cinema releases recover their production costs and turn a profit, adding that producers can still fail to recoup their investment after spending heavily on advertising and promotion. item.title: Casualties feared as multi-storey building collapses in Nairobi
item.description: A multi-storey building collapsed mid-construction in the Kenyan capital on Friday, the Red Cross said, with reports from local media of casualties and looting at the site. Videos spreading online showed a dramatic crash and huge clouds of dust as the building came down in a busy business and residential district. “At around 1340 hours, a multi-storey building under construction collapsed on 9th Street in Eastleigh, Nairobi,” the Red Cross posted on X, adding that it had dispatched a team. Local media reported looting and possible casualties trapped beneath the rubble, with images showing large crowds gathered at the site. There were conflicting reports on the size of the building, which may have been as high as 18 storeys. Eastleigh is a densely packed residential and market area, known as a hub for the Somali community. Nairobi is undergoing an extremely rapid construction boom, with high-rise buildings appearing all over the city as Kenya’s population expands. item.description: Bottled water: check. Torch: check. Blankets: check. UK leader Andy Burnham said Britons need to be better prepared for emergencies on Friday, when he hosted a wildfire and resilience summit. The prime minister highlighted a new government campaign that urges households to stockpile essential items in case everyday services are disrupted by anything from severe weather to cyberattacks. The “Be Ready” initiative advises storing three days’ worth of bottled water and non-perishable food, a battery or wind-up FM radio to receive updates during outages, and banknotes and coins in case electronic payments or cash machines are disrupted. Sleeping bags, spare batteries and toiletries are also on the checklist, which was published on Thursday and is in line with guidance issued in France, Ireland and The Netherlands. “We’re having the conversation with people about being better prepared because we’re living in a world where unexpected events seem to be becoming more and more common,” said Burnham, giving storms as an example. “It is just having those supplies in the house to get you through those moments. item.title: Nigerian man dies in sleep in UK; leaves wife, two children
item.description: The Nigerian Community in the United Kingdom has announced the death of a Nigerian man, Ekeobong Omega Nelson, who died at the age of 35, leaving behind his wife and two young children. item.description: A caregiver wore a protective gown and gloves as she bottle-fed a baby — one of hundreds of children orphaned by the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ebola outbreak. The mining town in Ituri province near the Uganda border is considered the epicentre of the outbreak. Children account for about one-third of deaths and more than one-quarter of infections in the current crisis — more than 2,000 cases, according to UNICEF.
